user.title: Inverter Charge Night – Entities
user.description: Step 1 of 4: Choose the operation mode and the inverter, forecast and battery entities. Night Charge charges the battery from the grid during the time window; Morning Discharge discharges it before sunrise to make room for solar production.

data_description.name: Name for this integration instance
data_description.operation_mode: Night charge fills the battery from the grid during the cheap window, sized so that tomorrow's PV still fits. Morning discharge is the opposite, and experimental: on a summer day whose forecast covers the house anyway, it empties the battery into the morning peak - roughly 05:00 to 08:00, when households draw the most and the sun is not up yet. That earns the spread on a dynamic tariff and takes load off the grid at its tightest hour. It needs a force discharge switch and a tariff that pays for it. If in doubt, stay on Night charge. See docs/morning-discharge.md.
data_description.min_soc_entity: The inverter's number entity for the minimum state of charge. It also identifies this instance, so each inverter can only be configured once.
data_description.grid_charge_switch: The inverter's switch that turns charging from the grid on and off.
data_description.pv_forecast_entity: PV forecast for the NEXT DAY (e.g. sensor.solcast_forecast_tomorrow). Used automatically when the window runs before midnight (evening). Also used as fallback if today's forecast entity is not configured. Do not select an ICN output such as Evening outlook or Target SoC.
data_description.pv_forecast_today_entity: Optional: TODAY's PV forecast entity (e.g. sensor.solcast_forecast_today). Used automatically when the window runs after midnight. Falls back to the main forecast entity if not set. The evening outlook and the curtailment outlook need it and stay empty without it.
data_description.battery_soc_entity: Select the sensor that shows current battery state of charge (%)
data_description.battery_capacity: Capacity corresponding to 0–100% of the reported SoC, before the configured SoC reserve. For 35.8 kWh and an 8% floor, 32.936 kWh remain above the reserve. Do not subtract this reserve twice. If the manufacturer normalizes SoC to an already usable range, use the capacity for that range.

time_soc.title: Inverter Charge Night – Time & SOC
time_soc.description: Step 2 of 4: Set the time window in which the integration is active and the SOC limits. The calculated target SOC is always kept between the minimum and the maximum. All times use the Home Assistant time zone, including daylight saving time. Every section can be revisited before saving.

data.default_min_soc: Fallback minimum SOC when restoring inverter settings
data.forecast_error_margin: Additional battery headroom for PV generation

data_description.start_time: Time when the window should start. Hour:minute, 24-hour format. The window may span midnight (e.g., 22:00 to 05:59).
data_description.end_time: Time when the window should end and settings are reset. Hour:minute, 24-hour format. The window may span midnight.
data_description.user_min_soc: Minimum allowed SOC percentage (0-100). Target SOC will not go below this.
data_description.user_max_soc: Maximum allowed SOC percentage (0-100). Target SOC will not go above this.
data_description.default_min_soc: ICN normally restores the minimum SOC read before charging. This fallback is used only when that original value is unavailable. New setups initially use the chosen target minimum, e.g. 8%.
data_description.forecast_error_margin: Increases assumed PV yield by this percentage. Example: a 10 kWh forecast plus 10% reserves space for 11 kWh. More PV headroom can lower the night charging target. Use bridge reserve to allow additional morning energy.
data_description.planner_mode: Bridge: also plans energy from the end of the charging window until sufficient PV production, using learned/average household load and sunrise plus the delay in Advanced. PV headroom: only leaves room for the forecast; it does not additionally cover morning consumption.
data_description.high_price_start: Optional: the time from which buying from the grid costs more than usual — a §14a peak period, or the evening block of a dynamic tariff (often 18:00). The planner then makes sure the battery can carry the house through it: what the house will draw between these two times, minus what tomorrow's sun is forecast to put in, is bought in tonight's cheap window. Leave both empty if you have no such period.
data_description.high_price_end: The time the high-price period is over (often 21:00). May run past midnight. Either set both times or neither — one end alone says when it starts but never when it stops.
data_description.high_price_margin_pct: The reserve is worked out from the learned house load profile, which is an average of the last days — an evening with the oven and the washing machine lies above it. This adds that percentage on top. 0 % takes the average at face value.

power.title: Inverter Charge Night – Charge Power
power.description: Charging power and optional features. Measurement sensors may stay empty without efficiency search. With efficiency search, the ceiling and both power sensors are required; an incomplete submission marks them as required. The additional AC/DC ceiling is an independent pair and may stay completely empty.

data.charge_power_entity: Battery Max AC Charge Limit Entity
data.charge_power_received_entity: Charge power arriving in the battery
data.charge_energy_received_entity: Energy meter: stored in the battery
data.force_discharge_switch: Force discharge switch (required for Morning discharge)

data_description.min_charge_power_w: Minimum charge power allowed for AUTO mode (W).
data_description.max_charge_power_w: Maximum charge power allowed for AUTO mode (W).
data_description.absolute_max_charge_power_w: Additional device-wide AC/DC charging ceiling, only together with the separate control entity below. Not required for normal planning or efficiency search. Leave both fields empty if the inverter has no separate total-charge control.
data_description.absolute_max_charge_power_entity: Only required when the additional AC/DC ceiling above is set. A separate charging ceiling in W; neither percent-based Active Power Setpoint nor the same entity as the normal charge ceiling.
data_description.charge_power_entity: Writable battery charge ceiling with readback in W. Required for efficiency search or house-connection limiting. With KORE use Battery Max Charge Limit (Modbus), never the percent-based Active Power Setpoint.
data_description.charge_power_sent_entity: Required for efficiency search: dedicated AC power entering the battery, positive during charging (KORE: Grid to Battery Power). Total inverter AC power, household consumption and net grid import are unsuitable.
data_description.charge_power_received_entity: Required for efficiency search: DC power reaching the battery, positive during charging (KORE: Battery Power; verify the sign). Select a separate measurement from AC input power.
data_description.charge_energy_sent_entity: Optional but better: a kWh meter of the energy the charger takes in. With both meters the efficiency search measures the energy that really flowed instead of integrating a power reading.
data_description.charge_energy_received_entity: Optional: the matching kWh meter on the battery side. Only useful together with the meter above.
data_description.auto_efficient_charge: Tests permitted charging powers and compares AC input energy with stored DC energy. Requires a watt-based ceiling and two suitable power sensors. Results need actual measurement time, sufficient energy and plausible feedback. Load limits and safety stops take priority.
data_description.force_discharge_switch: Switch entity that makes the inverter discharge the battery into the grid (e.g. via Modbus). Required in Morning discharge mode - it is the only thing that actually discharges; unused in Night charge mode.
data_description.discharge_limit_entity: Optional: number entity for the battery discharge power limit (W or kW). Set to 0 at the window start so the house runs from the grid and stored PV is kept; the previous value is restored at the window end.
data_description.grid_import_entity: Current import from the grid in W (or kW). Without this entity the charge power is not limited against the house connection.
data_description.main_fuse_a: Main fuse of the house connection, per phase. 63 A on three phases is about 43 kW of nominal power. Needed unless you enter the maximum continuous power below.
data_description.grid_phases: 1 for a single-phase connection, 3 for a three-phase one.
data_description.grid_voltage_v: Phase voltage of your grid, 230 V in Germany. Used together with the fuse size to work out the nominal power.
data_description.grid_continuous_pct: Share of the nominal power that may be drawn for hours on end. 80 % leaves room for the heating of meter and terminal contacts; pick a lower value for an older meter.
data_description.grid_max_continuous_w: Enter the continuous budget directly instead of the fuse size. Takes precedence when set.
data_description.grid_headroom_w: Distance kept below the budget, so a load the battery cannot see coming does not push the connection over the limit.
data_description.discharge_block_switch: Optional: switch entity of the inverter that blocks battery discharge (Kostal calls it "battery discharge lock"). Preferred over every other way; turned on at the window start and put back to its previous state at the window end.
data_description.discharge_block_mode: Blocks the battery from discharging into the house during the window, so stored energy is kept for the day. A switch of the inverter is preferred; if there is none, the integration raises the min SOC instead and resets it at the window end.

advanced.title: Inverter Charge Night – Advanced
advanced.description: Step 4 of 4: Fine-tune the update interval and command delay, restrict the active date range and select a backup mode entity. The defaults are fine for most installations.

data.active_range_yearly: Repeat the date range every year
data.auto_pv_shortfall: Automatically allow for severe PV shortfalls

data_description.update_interval: How often the coordinator should refresh data (seconds, default 900)
data_description.command_delay: Delay between min SOC and grid charge commands (seconds, default 0.1)
data_description.active_start_date: Optional: only run between this date and end date (YYYY-MM-DD). Leave empty to always allow.
data_description.active_end_date: Optional: only run between start date and this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Leave empty to always allow.
data_description.active_range_yearly: On (recommended): only the day and month of the two dates above count, so the range comes back every year - a tariff season stands in a price sheet and holds until further notice. Off: the years count too, and the integration stops for good once the end date has passed. A range that crosses the new year (start after end, e.g. 1 November to 31 March) is always read as a season, because read absolutely it could not contain a single day.
data_description.backup_mode_entity: Optional but important: an entity that says whether the house is running on the battery instead of the grid. While it does, the integration changes nothing on the inverter - there is nothing to charge from, and a raised min SOC would stop the battery from supplying the house. A switch, a binary sensor, or a state sensor (see below). With a manual transfer switch, an input_boolean you flip yourself works just as well.
data_description.backup_mode_states: Only needed when the entity above is a plain sensor rather than a switch: the states that mean the house is running on the battery, comma separated. A Kostal inverter reports “ESB” (Ersatzstrombetrieb) in its inverter state. Leave empty for a switch or binary sensor - on means backup there.
data_description.house_load_entity: Optional: cumulative energy meter (kWh) of the house consumption. The Bridge planner learns an hourly load profile from the last 14 days of recorder statistics; without it the average load below is used.
data_description.avg_house_load_kw: Average house load in kW, used by the Bridge planner when no consumption meter is configured or no statistics are available yet (default 0.5).
data_description.pv_crossover_delay_min: Minutes after sunrise until the PV output exceeds the house load (default 90). The Bridge planner charges enough to bridge the window end until then.
data_description.bridge_reserve_kwh: Safety reserve in kWh added to the bridge energy (default 0.5).
data_description.charge_efficiency: Grid-to-battery charge efficiency (0.5-1.0, default 0.9), used to plan the charge power for the remaining window time.
data_description.discharge_efficiency: How much of what leaves the battery arrives in the house (0.5-1.0, default 0.95). The load profile and the forecast are measured on the house side; energy coming out of the battery loses a few percent on the way through the inverter. Without this the planner buys a little too little for the bridge and for the evening reserve - every night, in the same direction.
data_description.night_price_ct: Optional: electricity price during the window in ct/kWh. Set all three prices or none; the Bridge planner uses them to decide a conflict between bridging and PV headroom. With a price entity configured below, the entity supplies night and day and only the feed-in price is needed — these two then only serve as a fallback for whenever the entity cannot price both the window and the morning after it — before the next day's prices are published, during an ad-hoc window, and always in the morning-discharge mode, which has no morning to bridge.
data_description.day_price_ct: Optional: electricity price outside the window in ct/kWh (set together with the night price; with a price entity, both may be left empty).
data_description.feed_in_price_ct: Optional: feed-in tariff in ct/kWh. No price source publishes one, so this is always entered by hand — and with a price entity it is the only one of the three you need.
data_description.price_entity: Optional: a sensor whose attributes carry today's and tomorrow's hourly prices — Tibber, aWATTar, EPEX Spot, Nordpool, ENTSO-e and anything shaped like them. The integration does not need to know which one it is; it recognises the series by its shape and reports what it matched on the price sensor. Leave empty to keep using the three fixed prices above.
data_description.price_unit: Leave on 'detect automatically' unless the entity carries no unit, or carries one that is wrong. Nothing is ever guessed here: with no unit from the entity, the attribute name or this field, the price entity is refused and the fixed prices are used — a wrong guess would be a factor of a hundred.
data_description.price_surcharge_ct: What your bill adds on top of what the entity shows — grid fee, levies, taxes, VAT. Tibber already shows the full price, so leave this at 0. aWATTar, EPEX Spot, Nordpool and ENTSO-e usually show the exchange price alone; in Germany the difference is typically 20–25 ct/kWh. Getting this wrong does not look wrong — 6 ct and 32 ct are both plausible numbers, and the evening reserve comes out the other way round on the wrong one.
data_description.price_surcharge_window_ct: The same, for the hours of your cheap window — this is where a reduced §14a grid fee lives. Leave empty when the surcharge is the same around the clock.
data_description.curtailment_limit_w: Optional: the most your system is allowed to feed into the grid, in watts — the 60 % or 70 % limit at the grid connection point. Enter the cap itself, not the percentage: 0.60 x your array in watts, so 9000 for 15 kWp at 60 %. Leave empty if you are not capped. Nothing is throttled from this; it only tells you how much midday PV the cap throws away because the battery was already full.
data_description.curtailment_feed_in_entity: Optional: a power sensor for what actually goes out to the grid. The cap applies to this, so it is the one measurement that can check the figure above against reality — the curtailment sensor holds the modelled overflow next to the measured one. Without it the sensor is model-only and says so.
data_description.auto_pv_shortfall: Optional: compares a morning full-day forecast of at least 5 kWh with fresh daily energy after sunset. At 15% or less, the next regular night charges to your maximum SOC. Possible causes include snow, shading, equipment faults or a wrong forecast. Requires observing a complete day.
data_description.pv_energy_today_entity: Whole-array daily PV energy in Wh/kWh/MWh, reset every day. Use neither instantaneous power nor a lifetime counter. Also requires the forecast for today.

review.title: Review settings
review.description:
**{name}**

Charging window: **{start}–{end}**, time zone **{timezone}** (including DST).

Capacity: **{capacity} kWh**, floor **{floor}%**, approximately **{usable} kWh** above that floor.

Controls and measurement sources:
{controls}

Reopen any section to correct it; other entries are retained. Changes are applied only when saved. Run only one active battery controller per inverter.

basics.title: 1 · Inverter and battery
basics.description:
Select the four entities and enter the battery’s **gross capacity**. Matching entities are suggested when exactly one KostalKore inverter is found; verify them before saving. Choose a forecast integration’s sensor, not an ICN output. Only the charging window remains after this page. **The inverter is not changed yet.**

Entity IDs containing “kostal_lab” are examples; the prefix depends on your device name.

data_description.name: Any descriptive name, for example “House battery”. Does not rename inverter entities.
data_description.min_soc_entity: KostalKore: “Battery min SoC”, e.g. number.kostal_lab_battery_min_soc. Writable minimum SOC in %, not measured battery charge.
data_description.grid_charge_switch: KostalKore: “Battery Manual Charge”, e.g. switch.kostal_lab_battery_manual_charge. Enables charging from the public grid.
data_description.battery_soc_entity: KostalKore: “Battery SoC”, e.g. sensor.kostal_lab_battery_soc. Measured battery state of charge in %.
data_description.battery_capacity: Total nameplate capacity in kWh, not usable capacity. Example: 35.8 kWh gross at an 8% floor gives 32.936 kWh usable.
data_description.pv_forecast_entity: Tomorrow’s full-day PV forecast in kWh, e.g. sensor.solcast_pv_forecast_forecast_tomorrow (depends on forecast integration). KostalKore provides measurements, not weather forecasts. Do not select an ICN evening outlook.

schedule.title: 2 · Charging window and state of charge
schedule.description: Times use Home Assistant’s time zone **{timezone}**, including daylight saving time. The window can cross midnight, for example 23:01–04:58. Minimum and maximum bound the planned target; maximum does not mean charging to full every night. Saving returns to the overview.

data.user_min_soc: Lower bound for planned charging target
data.user_max_soc: Upper bound for planned charging target

data_description.start_time: Local time when ordinary grid charging is allowed to begin.
data_description.end_time: Local time when charging must end. For an overnight window, this is on the following day.
data_description.user_min_soc: The planned target cannot be lower than this percentage. Respect the battery’s technical minimum, e.g. 8%.
data_description.user_max_soc: The planned target cannot exceed this percentage. Use 100% for full capacity or your preferred lower ceiling.

charging.title: Limit charging power
charging.description:
Configure this when charging power is adjustable. Without a power control, the inverter determines charging power. These watt limits alone do not limit house import; configure the house connection limit too. KostalKore: Battery max charge limit (Modbus), **not Active Power Set Point in %**.

Entity IDs containing “kostal_lab” are examples; the prefix depends on your device name.

data_description.charge_power_entity: KostalKore: “Battery max charge limit (Modbus)”, e.g. number.kostal_lab_battery_max_charge_limit_modbus. Verified battery power ceiling in watts; availability depends on model. Active Power Set Point in % is unsuitable. The additional absolute ceiling is a different feature.
data_description.min_charge_power_w: Lowest stable and useful charging power. Charging pauses when remaining house headroom is lower.
data_description.max_charge_power_w: Upper bound for planning and efficiency search. Must not exceed inverter, battery and installation ratings. House connection limits apply additionally.

efficiency.title: Set up efficiency search
efficiency.description:
Saving enables automatic search. All five fields are required. Compare AC charging input with DC power received by the battery. KostalKore: **Grid to Battery Power** and **Battery Power**; **AC Power is inverter output and is unsuitable**. Verify measurement direction and boundaries. Search runs during suitable night charging, not immediately. Disable it under other features.

Entity IDs containing “kostal_lab” are examples; the prefix depends on your device name.

data.charge_power_sent_entity: AC input power used only for battery charging
data.charge_power_received_entity: DC charging power received by battery

data_description.charge_power_entity: KostalKore: “Battery max charge limit (Modbus)”, e.g. number.kostal_lab_battery_max_charge_limit_modbus. Verified battery power ceiling in watts; availability depends on model. Active Power Set Point in % is unsuitable. The additional absolute ceiling is a different feature.
data_description.charge_power_sent_entity: KostalKore: “Grid to Battery Power”, e.g. sensor.kostal_lab_grid_to_battery_power. Only AC used to charge the battery, not house import or inverter “AC Power”. PV must not add charging input during measurement.
data_description.charge_power_received_entity: KostalKore: “Battery Power”, e.g. sensor.kostal_lab_battery_power. DC charging power; the sign is handled. Must be separate from the AC input measurement.
data_description.min_charge_power_w: Lowest stable and useful charging power. Charging pauses when remaining house headroom is lower.
data_description.max_charge_power_w: Upper bound for planning and efficiency search. Must not exceed inverter, battery and installation ratings. House connection limits apply additionally.

meters.title: Efficiency measurements and energy meters
meters.description: Edit AC/DC power measurements here, or clear them with efficiency search disabled, without enabling search. Changing measurement bindings can require learning efficiency again. Energy counters must measure separate AC/DC battery charging energy: supply both in kWh or leave both empty. House consumption and PV daily counters are unsuitable.

data.charge_energy_received_entity: Energy meter: stored in the battery
data.charge_power_sent_entity: AC input power used only for battery charging
data.charge_power_received_entity: DC charging power received by battery

data_description.charge_energy_sent_entity: Optional but better: a kWh meter of the energy the charger takes in. With both meters the efficiency search measures the energy that really flowed instead of integrating a power reading.
data_description.charge_energy_received_entity: Optional: the matching kWh meter on the battery side. Only useful together with the meter above.
data_description.charge_power_sent_entity: KostalKore: “Grid to Battery Power”, e.g. sensor.kostal_lab_grid_to_battery_power. Only AC used to charge the battery, not house import or inverter “AC Power”. PV must not add charging input during measurement.
data_description.charge_power_received_entity: KostalKore: “Battery Power”, e.g. sensor.kostal_lab_battery_power. DC charging power; the sign is handled. Must be separate from the AC input measurement.

grid.title: Limit house connection import
grid.description: All four fields are required. Measure **total house grid import**, including cars, house and battery; import must be positive. Enter the permitted continuous import budget. Example: 40,000 W − 33,000 W cars − 1,000 W house = at most 6,000 W for battery charging, less safety headroom. A watt power control is required. Software does not replace electrical protection.

data_description.grid_import_entity: Total import measured at the house grid connection, positive in W or kW. Include battery and cars. The KostalKore meter and sign depend on model and must be verified.
data_description.grid_max_continuous_w: Continuous import budget in W shared by every consumer. Use the limit determined for the installation.
data_description.grid_headroom_w: Additional unused headroom in W, e.g. 500 W. Less available capacity reduces battery charging; below minimum charging power it pauses.
data_description.charge_power_entity: KostalKore: “Battery max charge limit (Modbus)”, e.g. number.kostal_lab_battery_max_charge_limit_modbus. Verified battery power ceiling in watts; availability depends on model. Active Power Set Point in % is unsuitable. The additional absolute ceiling is a different feature.

planning.title: PV forecast and morning reserve
planning.description: Optional planning adjustments. PV headroom leaves space for tomorrow’s generation. Bridge mode also accounts for house use between the charging window ending and PV meeting demand. Supply a house consumption energy meter or a realistic average load. Defaults are estimates.

data.forecast_error_margin: Additional battery headroom for PV generation
data.default_min_soc: Fallback minimum SOC when restoring inverter settings

data_description.planner_mode: Bridge mode also plans house consumption from the window ending until expected PV supply. Use the load and delay fields on this page. PV headroom reserves space for forecast generation without additionally planning morning use.
data_description.forecast_error_margin: Increases assumed PV yield by this percentage. Example: a 10 kWh forecast plus 10% reserves space for 11 kWh. More PV headroom can lower the night charging target. Use bridge reserve to allow additional morning energy.
data_description.default_min_soc: ICN normally restores the minimum SOC read before charging. This fallback is used only when that original value is unavailable. New setups initially use the chosen target minimum, e.g. 8%.
data_description.pv_forecast_today_entity: Today’s full-day energy forecast in kWh. Improves matching after midnight. Different from measured generation today.
data_description.house_load_entity: Optional: cumulative energy meter (kWh) of the house consumption. The Bridge planner learns an hourly load profile from the last 14 days of recorder statistics; without it the average load below is used.
data_description.avg_house_load_kw: Average house load in kW, used by the Bridge planner when no consumption meter is configured or no statistics are available yet (default 0.5).
data_description.pv_crossover_delay_min: Minutes after sunrise until the PV output exceeds the house load (default 90). The Bridge planner charges enough to bridge the window end until then.
data_description.bridge_reserve_kwh: Safety reserve in kWh added to the bridge energy (default 0.5).

evening.title: Reserve for expensive evening hours
evening.description: Use this to reserve energy for a fixed expensive period. Set both times or leave both empty to disable the evening reserve. Consumption history estimates demand. Without a discharge-block switch, the minimum SOC is used.

data_description.high_price_start: Optional: the time from which buying from the grid costs more than usual — a §14a peak period, or the evening block of a dynamic tariff (often 18:00). The planner then makes sure the battery can carry the house through it: what the house will draw between these two times, minus what tomorrow's sun is forecast to put in, is bought in tonight's cheap window. Leave both empty if you have no such period.
data_description.high_price_end: The time the high-price period is over (often 21:00). May run past midnight. Either set both times or neither — one end alone says when it starts but never when it stops.
data_description.high_price_margin_pct: The reserve is worked out from the learned house load profile, which is an average of the last days — an evening with the oven and the washing machine lies above it. This adds that percentage on top. 0 % takes the average at face value.
data_description.discharge_block_mode: Blocks the battery from discharging into the house during the window, so stored energy is kept for the day. A switch of the inverter is preferred; if there is none, the integration raises the min SOC instead and resets it at the window end.
data_description.discharge_block_switch: Optional: switch entity of the inverter that blocks battery discharge (Kostal calls it "battery discharge lock"). Preferred over every other way; turned on at the window start and put back to its previous state at the window end.

season.title: Active season
season.description: Leave both dates empty for year-round operation. For winter, use 1 October through 31 March with yearly repeat enabled. Seasons crossing New Year are supported.

data.active_range_yearly: Repeat the date range every year

data_description.active_start_date: Optional: only run between this date and end date (YYYY-MM-DD). Leave empty to always allow.
data_description.active_end_date: Optional: only run between start date and this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Leave empty to always allow.
data_description.active_range_yearly: On (recommended): only the day and month of the two dates above count, so the range comes back every year - a tariff season stands in a price sheet and holds until further notice. Off: the years count too, and the integration stops for good once the end date has passed. A range that crosses the new year (start after end, e.g. 1 November to 31 March) is always read as a season, because read absolutely it could not contain a single day.

backup.title: Detect island operation
backup.description: Select a reliable island/backup status entity. Active or unavailable status prevents grid charging. Lab example: binary_sensor.icn_lab_charge_inhibit. Actual KostalKore availability and values depend on inverter model.

data_description.backup_mode_entity: Optional but important: an entity that says whether the house is running on the battery instead of the grid. While it does, the integration changes nothing on the inverter - there is nothing to charge from, and a raised min SOC would stop the battery from supplying the house. A switch, a binary sensor, or a state sensor (see below). With a manual transfer switch, an input_boolean you flip yourself works just as well.
data_description.backup_mode_states: Only needed when the entity above is a plain sensor rather than a switch: the states that mean the house is running on the battery, comma separated. A Kostal inverter reports “ESB” (Ersatzstrombetrieb) in its inverter state. Leave empty for a switch or binary sensor - on means backup there.

pv_shortfall.title: Account for very low PV yield
pv_shortfall.description: Saving enables this feature. Both sensors are required: today’s full-day forecast and actual PV energy generated today in kWh. A severe deficit after sunset raises the next night’s target to your maximum and produces a notice. This detects poor yield, not its cause.

data_description.pv_forecast_today_entity: Today’s full-day energy forecast in kWh. Improves matching after midnight. Different from measured generation today.
data_description.pv_energy_today_entity: Whole-array daily PV energy in Wh/kWh/MWh, reset every day. Use neither instantaneous power nor a lifetime counter. Also requires the forecast for today.

prices.title: Account for electricity prices
prices.description: Defaults are sufficient for ordinary operation. Enter all three fixed tariffs together. With a dynamic price sensor, only the feed-in tariff is additionally needed. Electrical limits always take precedence.

data_description.night_price_ct: Optional: electricity price during the window in ct/kWh. Set all three prices or none; the Bridge planner uses them to decide a conflict between bridging and PV headroom. With a price entity configured below, the entity supplies night and day and only the feed-in price is needed — these two then only serve as a fallback for whenever the entity cannot price both the window and the morning after it — before the next day's prices are published, during an ad-hoc window, and always in the morning-discharge mode, which has no morning to bridge.
data_description.day_price_ct: Optional: electricity price outside the window in ct/kWh (set together with the night price; with a price entity, both may be left empty).
data_description.feed_in_price_ct: Optional: feed-in tariff in ct/kWh. No price source publishes one, so this is always entered by hand — and with a price entity it is the only one of the three you need.
data_description.price_entity: Optional: a sensor whose attributes carry today's and tomorrow's hourly prices — Tibber, aWATTar, EPEX Spot, Nordpool, ENTSO-e and anything shaped like them. The integration does not need to know which one it is; it recognises the series by its shape and reports what it matched on the price sensor. Leave empty to keep using the three fixed prices above.
data_description.price_unit: Leave on 'detect automatically' unless the entity carries no unit, or carries one that is wrong. Nothing is ever guessed here: with no unit from the entity, the attribute name or this field, the price entity is refused and the fixed prices are used — a wrong guess would be a factor of a hundred.
data_description.price_surcharge_ct: What your bill adds on top of what the entity shows — grid fee, levies, taxes, VAT. Tibber already shows the full price, so leave this at 0. aWATTar, EPEX Spot, Nordpool and ENTSO-e usually show the exchange price alone; in Germany the difference is typically 20–25 ct/kWh. Getting this wrong does not look wrong — 6 ct and 32 ct are both plausible numbers, and the evening reserve comes out the other way round on the wrong one.
data_description.price_surcharge_window_ct: The same, for the hours of your cheap window — this is where a reduced §14a grid fee lives. Leave empty when the surcharge is the same around the clock.

hardware.title: Additional hardware limits
hardware.description: Only configure verified hardware functions. The additional absolute ceiling needs both a value and its own, separate control entity. A direct house import budget in watts takes precedence over the fuse calculation.

data.absolute_max_charge_power_entity: Additional hardware ceiling: separate watt control

data_description.absolute_max_charge_power_entity: Usually leave empty. Only for an additional independent hardware ceiling; never reuse the ordinary charging control.
data_description.absolute_max_charge_power_w: Usually leave empty. Supply only together with its separate hardware control.
data_description.discharge_limit_entity: Optional: number entity for the battery discharge power limit (W or kW). Set to 0 at the window start so the house runs from the grid and stored PV is kept; the previous value is restored at the window end.

runtime.title: Other settings
runtime.description: Settings for special installations and operating modes. Keep night charging selected for ordinary use. Morning discharge requires a dedicated force-discharge switch. Only change efficiency and curtailment settings when their meaning for your system is known.

data.force_discharge_switch: Force discharge switch (required for Morning discharge)

data_description.update_interval: How often the coordinator should refresh data (seconds, default 900)
data_description.command_delay: Delay between min SOC and grid charge commands (seconds, default 0.1)
data_description.charge_efficiency: Grid-to-battery charge efficiency (0.5-1.0, default 0.9), used to plan the charge power for the remaining window time.
data_description.discharge_efficiency: How much of what leaves the battery arrives in the house (0.5-1.0, default 0.95). The load profile and the forecast are measured on the house side; energy coming out of the battery loses a few percent on the way through the inverter. Without this the planner buys a little too little for the bridge and for the evening reserve - every night, in the same direction.
data_description.curtailment_feed_in_entity: Optional: a power sensor for what actually goes out to the grid. The cap applies to this, so it is the one measurement that can check the figure above against reality — the curtailment sensor holds the modelled overflow next to the measured one. Without it the sensor is model-only and says so.
data_description.curtailment_limit_w: Optional: the most your system is allowed to feed into the grid, in watts — the 60 % or 70 % limit at the grid connection point. Enter the cap itself, not the percentage: 0.60 x your array in watts, so 9000 for 15 kWp at 60 %. Leave empty if you are not capped. Nothing is throttled from this; it only tells you how much midday PV the cap throws away because the battery was already full.
data_description.operation_mode: Night charge fills the battery from the grid during the cheap window, sized so that tomorrow's PV still fits. Morning discharge is the opposite, and experimental: on a summer day whose forecast covers the house anyway, it empties the battery into the morning peak - roughly 05:00 to 08:00, when households draw the most and the sun is not up yet. That earns the spread on a dynamic tariff and takes load off the grid at its tightest hour. It needs a force discharge switch and a tariff that pays for it. If in doubt, stay on Night charge. See docs/morning-discharge.md.
data_description.force_discharge_switch: Switch entity that makes the inverter discharge the battery into the grid (e.g. via Modbus). Required in Morning discharge mode - it is the only thing that actually discharges; unused in Night charge mode.

setup.description:
**ICN 3.10 · Setup overview**

Start with **1. Inverter and battery** and **2. Charging window**. Then review and apply. Basic fields present: **{core_count}/6**.

Each submitted page is saved as a draft and returns here. Reopen any section to go back and edit it. Save and close to pause; resume from the same setup later. Drafts are kept for 30 days. Unsubmitted browser inputs are not saved. Only Apply changes the running configuration.

Home Assistant time zone: **{timezone}**.

**{name}**

Charging window **{start}–{end}**, time zone **{timezone}**.

Battery **{capacity} kWh gross**, fallback discharge floor **{floor}%**, calculated usable energy above it **{usable} kWh**.

Planned target bounds: **{target_min}–{target_max}%**.

resume_draft.title: Resume saved draft
resume_draft.description: Select a saved draft. Timestamps are UTC. Unapplied settings do not control the inverter.

grid_fuse.title: Calculate import budget from fuse rating
grid_fuse.description: Alternative to a direct watt budget. All fields are required. Budget is phases × voltage × fuse current × continuous-load percentage. Saving removes a prior direct watt budget. Use ratings determined for your installation.

data_description.grid_import_entity: Total import measured at the house grid connection, positive in W or kW. Include battery and cars. The KostalKore meter and sign depend on model and must be verified.
data_description.charge_power_entity: KostalKore: “Battery max charge limit (Modbus)”, e.g. number.kostal_lab_battery_max_charge_limit_modbus. Verified battery power ceiling in watts; availability depends on model. Active Power Set Point in % is unsuitable. The additional absolute ceiling is a different feature.
data_description.main_fuse_a: Main fuse of the house connection, per phase. 63 A on three phases is about 43 kW of nominal power. Needed unless you enter the maximum continuous power below.
data_description.grid_phases: 1 for a single-phase connection, 3 for a three-phase one.
data_description.grid_voltage_v: Phase voltage of your grid, 230 V in Germany. Used together with the fuse size to work out the nominal power.
data_description.grid_continuous_pct: Share of the nominal power that may be drawn for hours on end. 80 % leaves room for the heating of meter and terminal contacts; pick a lower value for an older meter.
data_description.grid_headroom_w: Additional unused headroom in W, e.g. 500 W. Less available capacity reduces battery charging; below minimum charging power it pauses.

disable_features.title: Disable features
disable_features.description: Changes the draft first. Apply settings to change the running configuration.

charging_off.title: Remove charging power control
charging_off.description: Disable efficiency search and house import limiting first. They require a watt control. Continue returns to feature selection. Active configuration changes only when finally applied.

init.title: Settings – Entities
init.description: Step 1 of 4: Update the operation mode and the inverter, forecast and battery entities. Night Charge charges the battery from the grid during the time window; Morning Discharge discharges it before sunrise to make room for solar production.

data_description.name: Name for this integration instance
data_description.operation_mode: Night charge fills the battery from the grid during the cheap window, sized so that tomorrow's PV still fits. Morning discharge is the opposite, and experimental: on a summer day whose forecast covers the house anyway, it empties the battery into the morning peak - roughly 05:00 to 08:00, when households draw the most and the sun is not up yet. That earns the spread on a dynamic tariff and takes load off the grid at its tightest hour. It needs a force discharge switch and a tariff that pays for it. If in doubt, stay on Night charge. See docs/morning-discharge.md.
data_description.min_soc_entity: The inverter's number entity for the minimum state of charge. It also identifies this instance, so each inverter can only be configured once.
data_description.grid_charge_switch: The inverter's switch that turns charging from the grid on and off.
data_description.pv_forecast_entity: PV forecast for the NEXT DAY (e.g. sensor.solcast_forecast_tomorrow). Used automatically when the window runs before midnight (evening). Also used as fallback if today's forecast entity is not configured. Do not select an ICN output such as Evening outlook or Target SoC.
data_description.pv_forecast_today_entity: Optional: TODAY's PV forecast entity (e.g. sensor.solcast_forecast_today). Used automatically when the window runs after midnight. Falls back to the main forecast entity if not set. The evening outlook and the curtailment outlook need it and stay empty without it.
data_description.battery_soc_entity: Select the sensor that shows current battery state of charge (%)
data_description.battery_capacity: Capacity corresponding to 0–100% of the reported SoC, before the configured SoC reserve. For 35.8 kWh and an 8% floor, 32.936 kWh remain above the reserve. Do not subtract this reserve twice. If the manufacturer normalizes SoC to an already usable range, use the capacity for that range.

time_soc.title: Settings – Time & SOC
time_soc.description: Step 2 of 4: Update the time window and the SOC limits. The calculated target SOC is always kept between the minimum and the maximum. All times use the Home Assistant time zone, including daylight saving time. Every section can be revisited before saving.

data.default_min_soc: Fallback minimum SOC when restoring inverter settings
data.forecast_error_margin: Additional battery headroom for PV generation

data_description.start_time: Time when the window should start. Hour:minute, 24-hour format. The window may span midnight (e.g., 22:00 to 05:59).
data_description.end_time: Time when the window should end and settings are reset. Hour:minute, 24-hour format. The window may span midnight.
data_description.user_min_soc: Minimum allowed SOC percentage (0-100). Target SOC will not go below this.
data_description.user_max_soc: Maximum allowed SOC percentage (0-100). Target SOC will not go above this.
data_description.default_min_soc: ICN normally restores the minimum SOC read before charging. This fallback is used only when that original value is unavailable. New setups initially use the chosen target minimum, e.g. 8%.
data_description.forecast_error_margin: Increases assumed PV yield by this percentage. Example: a 10 kWh forecast plus 10% reserves space for 11 kWh. More PV headroom can lower the night charging target. Use bridge reserve to allow additional morning energy.
data_description.planner_mode: Bridge: also plans energy from the end of the charging window until sufficient PV production, using learned/average household load and sunrise plus the delay in Advanced. PV headroom: only leaves room for the forecast; it does not additionally cover morning consumption.
data_description.high_price_start: Optional: the time from which buying from the grid costs more than usual — a §14a peak period, or the evening block of a dynamic tariff (often 18:00). The planner then makes sure the battery can carry the house through it: what the house will draw between these two times, minus what tomorrow's sun is forecast to put in, is bought in tonight's cheap window. Leave both empty if you have no such period.
data_description.high_price_end: The time the high-price period is over (often 21:00). May run past midnight. Either set both times or neither — one end alone says when it starts but never when it stops.
data_description.high_price_margin_pct: The reserve is worked out from the learned house load profile, which is an average of the last days — an evening with the oven and the washing machine lies above it. This adds that percentage on top. 0 % takes the average at face value.

power.title: Settings – Charge Power
power.description: Charging power and optional features. Measurement sensors may stay empty without efficiency search. With efficiency search, the ceiling and both power sensors are required; an incomplete submission marks them as required. The additional AC/DC ceiling is an independent pair and may stay completely empty.

data.charge_power_entity: Battery Max AC Charge Limit Entity
data.charge_power_received_entity: Charge power arriving in the battery

data_description.min_charge_power_w: Minimum charge power allowed for AUTO mode (W).

data_description.charge_energy_received_entity: Optional: the matching kWh meter on the battery side. Only useful together with the meter above.

data_description.grid_import_entity: Current import from the grid in W (or kW). Without this entity the charge power is not limited against the house connection.
data_description.main_fuse_a: Main fuse of the house connection, per phase. 63 A on three phases is about 43 kW of nominal power. Needed unless you enter the maximum continuous power below.
data_description.grid_phases: 1 for a single-phase connection, 3 for a three-phase one.
data_description.grid_voltage_v: Phase voltage of your grid, 230 V in Germany. Used together with the fuse size to work out the nominal power.
data_description.grid_continuous_pct: Share of the nominal power that may be drawn for hours on end. 80 % leaves room for the heating of meter and terminal contacts; pick a lower value for an older meter.

data_description.grid_headroom_w: Distance kept below the budget, so a load the battery cannot see coming does not push the connection over the limit.
data_description.discharge_block_switch: Optional: switch entity of the inverter that blocks battery discharge (Kostal calls it "battery discharge lock"). Preferred over every other way; turned on at the window start and put back to its previous state at the window end.

data_description.update_interval: How often the coordinator should refresh data (seconds, default 900)
data_description.command_delay: Delay between min SOC and grid charge commands (seconds, default 0.1)
data_description.active_start_date: Optional: only run between this date and end date (YYYY-MM-DD). Leave empty to always allow.
data_description.active_end_date: Optional: only run between start date and this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Leave empty to always allow.
data_description.active_range_yearly: On (recommended): only the day and month of the two dates above count, so the range comes back every year - a tariff season stands in a price sheet and holds until further notice. Off: the years count too, and the integration stops for good once the end date has passed. data_description.avg_house_load_kw: Average house load in kW, used by the Bridge planner when no consumption meter is configured or no statistics are available yet (default 0.5).
data_description.pv_crossover_delay_min: Minutes after sunrise until the PV output exceeds the house load (default 90). The Bridge planner charges enough to bridge the window end until then.
data_description.bridge_reserve_kwh: Safety reserve in kWh added to the bridge energy (default 0.5).
data_description.charge_efficiency: Grid-to-battery charge efficiency (0.5-1.0, default 0.9), used to plan the charge power for the remaining window time.
data_description.discharge_efficiency: How much of what leaves the battery arrives in the house (0.5-1.0, default 0.95). grid_fuse.title: Calculate import budget from fuse rating
grid_fuse.description: Alternative to a direct watt budget. All fields are required. Budget is phases × voltage × fuse current × continuous-load percentage. Saving removes a prior direct watt budget. Use ratings determined for your installation.

data_description.grid_import_entity: Total import measured at the house grid connection, positive in W or kW. Include battery and cars. The KostalKore meter and sign depend on model and must be verified.
data_description.charge_power_entity: KostalKore: “Battery max charge limit (Modbus)”, e.g. number.kostal_lab_battery_max_charge_limit_modbus. Verified battery power ceiling in watts; availability depends on model. Active Power Set Point in % is unsuitable. The additional absolute ceiling is a different feature.
data_description.main_fuse_a: Main fuse of the house connection, per phase. 63 A on three phases is about 43 kW of nominal power. Needed unless you enter the maximum continuous power below.
data_description.grid_phases: 1 for a single-phase connection, 3 for a three-phase one.
data_description.grid_voltage_v: Phase voltage of your grid, 230 V in Germany. Used together with the fuse size to work out the nominal power.
data_description.grid_continuous_pct: Share of the nominal power that may be drawn for hours on end. 80 % leaves room for the heating of meter and terminal contacts; pick a lower value for an older meter.
data_description.grid_headroom_w: Additional unused headroom in W, e.g. 500 W. Less available capacity reduces battery charging; below minimum charging power it pauses.

discharge_block_without_backup.title: {name}: the battery cannot supply the house during a power cut
discharge_block_without_backup.description:
To keep the energy it bought, this integration raises the inverter's minimum SOC while the window is open - and a battery does not discharge below its minimum SOC. If the power fails during the window and your house switches to the battery, the battery will refuse to supply it, however full it is.

Two ways out, either is enough:

1. Set **Backup / island mode entity** in the integration options (step 4). Any entity that says the house is running on the battery: the inverter's state sensor (a Kostal reports `ESB` - add it under **Backup mode states**), a binary sensor, or an `input_boolean` you flip yourself when you operate a manual transfer switch. The integration then hands the inverter back within seconds.

2. Set **Discharge block** to `Off` in step 3. The battery may then run the house at night, which costs the difference between the window tariff and the day tariff.

This message disappears once either is done.

active_range_expired.title: {name}: the active date range ended on {end_date}
active_range_expired.description:
The integration is configured to run only until {end_date}, and that date has passed - so it does not charge any more, and it will not start again on its own.

Three ways out, whichever fits:

1. Switch on **Repeat the date range every year** in the options (step 4). The range then means the day and month only, and comes back every year - which is what a tariff season usually is.
2. Enter a new end date.
3. Clear both dates to run all year round.

This message disappears as soon as one of them is done.
